scenes.title:
Your team.
Ready to race.
lines: A guide to your Team Garage
Portfolios · Media · Schedule · Results

scenes.title:
Start in
your garage.
lines: Sign in with the email linked to your team.
Check your team name, number and event.
The dashboard brings your deadlines and progress together.

scenes.title:
Upload your
portfolios.
lines: Open Submissions and choose a category.
Design & Engineering, Enterprise and Project Management each need a PDF.
Choose the file, then select Upload file.

scenes.title:
Check the
receipt.
lines: Each portfolio can be up to 12 MB.
Check Submission status after uploading.
Email confirmation status is separate from upload success.

scenes.title:
Know the
deadline.
lines: Portfolio deadlines are shown in IST.
At 5 points per started hour, 61 minutes late means 10 points.
Your first successful upload stops the clock; replacements keep that receipt.
scenes.cue: Check the deadline and rate shown for your event.

scenes.title:
Prepare your
media pack.
lines: Use the eight-item compulsory media checklist.
Submit the logo, both car renders, 3D model and materials.
Also complete the team photo, colours and member portraits.

scenes.title:
Add your
official photo.
lines: Upload a clear JPG or PNG, up to 25 MB.
4K or higher is recommended.
Confirm the required team and parent/guardian consent before uploading.

scenes.title:
Follow your
team schedule.
lines: Open My Schedule for your allocated stream.
Read the exact appointment time and location.
Only the published schedule is visible here; refresh for updates.

scenes.title:
Raise concerns.
Follow replies.
lines: Open Team feedback and select the relevant panel.
Describe what happened clearly.
Your team managers can follow the organiser’s response.

scenes.title:
Results arrive
after release.
lines: Open Results when the event team announces release.
Your scores and judging feedback appear there.
Until then, the page explains that results are not yet available.

scenes.title:
Ready for
competition.
lines: Three portfolio receipts checked.
Eight media deliverables completed.
Published schedule checked.
scenes.cue: Keep your team details and submissions up to date.

scenes.title:
Judge with
confidence.
lines: Assigned teams · Rubrics · Feedback
Submission · Scores · Lead moderation

scenes.title:
Open your
assignments.
lines: Go to My scorecards after signing in.
You can score only the teams explicitly assigned to your panel.
If a team is missing, ask an organiser to update your assignment.

scenes.title:
Declare any
conflict first.
lines: Use “I have a conflict with this team” when needed.
Confirm the declaration before scoring.
A conflict blocks judging for that team; ask the Chair if it was a mistake.

scenes.title:
Use the rubric
for every mark.
lines: Open the correct team and scorecard area.
Read the band descriptions before choosing a score.
Use the score buttons or enter a whole number within the allowed range.

scenes.title:
Give useful
team feedback.
lines: Complete the Overall Comment.
Add specific strengths and improvements.
Team feedback is shared after results are released.

scenes.title:
Keep private
notes separate.
lines: Internal notes are for the permitted judging and moderation views.
Use team-facing feedback for advice you want the team to receive.
Star Quality nominations inform a shortlist; they do not select winners.

scenes.title:
Check. Then
submit.
lines: Wait until scores, notes and feedback are saved.
Choose Check card and review every mark and the total.
Select Submit scorecard only when the card is ready.

scenes.title:
Drafts do
not count.
lines: Use Scores to check saved and submitted status.
A saved draft is still unfinished.
Only submitted cards contribute to Rankings.

scenes.title:
Lead judges:
reopen a card.
lines: In Moderation, select the area in your own panel.
Enter a reason beside the submitted scorecard.
Select Reopen so its judge can edit and submit again.

scenes.title:
Reopened means
review again.
lines: The card returns to draft and stops counting until resubmitted.
Lead Judges reopen only within their assigned panel.
Released results must be withdrawn before reopening is allowed.

scenes.title:
Before you
finish judging.
lines: Check every assigned scorecard is submitted.
Confirm feedback has saved.
Use Results for the officially released outcome.
scenes.cue: If an assignment or score needs attention, contact your panel lead.

scenes.title:
Run the event.
One workspace.
lines: People · Submissions · Streams
Scheduling · Racing · Results

scenes.title:
Confirm teams
and access.
lines: Review team numbers, names and manager details in Teams.
Use People to invite officials, judges and managers.
Invitees verify the same email to receive their role.

scenes.title:
Assign judges
to actual teams.
lines: In People → Judge assignments, choose the person and panel.
Select the team scope and save it.
“All current teams” does not automatically include later registrations.

scenes.title:
Keep roles
clear.
lines: Organisers manage event operations. Chairs control adjudication and release.
Only the platform owner manages hidden accounts and Platform Spectators.
Spectators can view organiser information but cannot change it.
scenes.cue: Hidden account identities are visible only to the platform owner.

scenes.title:
Set portfolio
deadlines.
lines: Open Submissions → Submission deadlines and penalties.
Set each deadline in IST and save the hourly rate.
At 5 points per started hour, missing or late portfolios accrue automatically.

scenes.title:
Review the
media assets.
lines: Track the eight compulsory deliverables in Submissions.
Use Media Assets to process and review team-photo cutouts.
Approve suitable cutouts for broadcast use; review failed jobs.

scenes.title:
Set up the
event day.
lines: Open Scheduling & Streams → Event setup.
Set the timezone, event dates and operating hours.
Add the rooms, judging panels and tracks used by your schedule.

scenes.title:
Allocate your
streams.
lines: Generate and inspect the random stream allocation preview.
Each stream holds a maximum of 10 teams.
Use Transfer team for adjustments; save the draft when ready.

scenes.title:
Build the
master timeline.
lines: Add ceremonies, activities, judging and racing.
Use All Streams for a shared ceremony.
Use individual team appointments for required judging and racing times.

scenes.title:
Generate exact
appointments.
lines: Expand Generate team appointment slots.
Set the start, duration, gap, order and appointments per team.
Choose the room or track, then generate and review the preview.
scenes.cue: Master schedule → Generate team appointment slots

scenes.title:
Resolve checks.
Publish deliberately.
lines: Review blocking conflicts and resource warnings.
Judging exemptions can cover one category or all judging.
Save draft first. Publish schedule makes the version visible to teams.
scenes.cue: Save draft → Check validation → Publish schedule

scenes.title:
Run and record
the racing.
lines: Use Race control to queue pairings and record lane results.
Check team, car, status and timings before saving.
Lane swaps and reruns stay linked to their source race.

scenes.title:
Follow scores
and concerns.
lines: Use Scores to find missing or draft cards.
Panel leads reopen their panel’s cards; the Chair handles score overrides.
Resolve reported concerns through Team feedback.

scenes.title:
Send clear
announcements.
lines: Open Communications and choose the intended audience.
Write the subject and message, then review the preview.
Check recipients before selecting Send announcement.

scenes.title:
Review rankings
before release.
lines: Check submitted cards, inspections, racing and penalties.
Resolve outstanding drafts, ties and event-completion checks.
A provisional ranking can still change.

scenes.title:
Publish, then
release results.
lines: The Chair publishes the current ranking snapshot.
Release results makes the official outcome visible to teams and the public.
Released results lock scoring and submission changes.

scenes.title:
Ready to run
race day.
lines: People assigned. Submissions checked.
Schedule published. Racing recorded.
Scores reviewed. Results released.
scenes.cue: Keep teams informed when official information changes.
